scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The garden picture
scenes.caption: Meera and Kabir photograph seedlings for their school garden magazine. The picture also shows full names on a noticeboard and where the club meets after school. Public readers need the garden story, but not those details.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A different audience
scenes.caption: The draft is shared with the class; the finished magazine will have a public link. Kabir assumes the same photo permission covers both. Meera notices the audience has changed. The pictured children have not agreed to public sharing.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Keep the purpose
scenes.caption: The story needs seedlings and care instructions, not names or a meeting location. Prepare a different picture, remove identifying details and check permission with the people pictured and the responsible teacher before publishing.
scenes.dialogue: Useful does not mean revealing everything.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Make the decision
scenes.caption: Choose the team's next step: publish the original, assume the class folder makes it safe, or prepare a suitable version and check permission. Test the plan by inspecting what a public reader can see.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A useful revision
scenes.caption: The new image explains the garden without showing children or the noticeboard. The teacher checks its public preview. This reduces unnecessary sharing. Editing a new version cannot remove copies of an old one already shared.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: A new screenshot
scenes.caption: Now inspect a sports-club screenshot. It includes contact details the teacher needs but the magazine does not. In the lab, prepare a safe image, test two sharing audiences and explain what should stay private.
